tasks.short: Run training sessions in different formats for shift crews.

today.trigger: A site manager, the annual plan, or an incident asks for a session on forklift, VCA, food safety, week-one induction, or a toolbox talk.
steps: Look up the Studytube course and the SharePoint procedure for that task.
Rebuild a PowerPoint or a spoken script from last year's file.
Fit the session around the shift in Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo, and book a room or a spot on the floor.
Lead the session: short explanation, role play or practice, questions.
Write down who was there so the completion or certificate can be recorded.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same deck for each site
Copying names into an attendance list
Rewriting a formal procedure into words a night shift will follow
today.time_sinks: The hour with the crew, plus waiting for a shift change or travelling between sites, is the bulk. Redoing materials for a topic that already exists sits on top.

lenses.faster: Role-play scripts, toolbox talks and slide drafts arrive from the approved procedure, so the rebuild before each session shrinks. The time with the crew stays.
lenses.autonomous: A booked Studytube session can open a format pack for that site and shift. Somebody still has to be in the room or on the floor.
lenses.ambitious: Each crew, including night shift and short-stay flex workers, would get this topic in a form they can use, on all three sites, rather than one classroom day in Rotterdam.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding last year's PowerPoint is the part nobody would miss. Reading the room, demonstrating the real task, and taking a question about yesterday's near-miss is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Five formats for one topic: toolbox talk, role play, supervised practice, short video for the shift that missed it, and a discussion for team leads.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the format menu and the rule for which crew gets which format, then checks whether people can do the task afterwards.
reach: Recruiter: a realistic job preview in the same formats, before offer
HR business partner: a ready manager workshop when a site asks for the same topic again
Team lead: a toolbox script they can run on the nights L&D is not on site

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether this crew understood, switching language level live, and showing a safety step that has to be seen.
tasks.pattern_why: The session is with people and carries safety liability, so the specialist stays in the lead and uses drafts only to prepare.

in_practice.trigger: A session is scheduled in Studytube, or a team lead asks for a toolbox talk.
steps: Pull the procedure, the audience (site, shift, permanent or flex, language) and any certificate rule.
Draft a toolbox script, a role play and a short discussion note in plain Dutch.
The specialist picks one, replaces generic examples with this site's layout, and runs the session.
Log attendance in Studytube and note what the crew could not do.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves the script and delivers the session. No material is used on a safety topic until a person has checked the steps.
data_needed: Approved procedure
Certificate rules for VCA, forklift and food safety
Site incident examples with names removed
Language and literacy notes per crew
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube attendance, plus a short session note on the SharePoint course folder.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts PowerPoint slides and speaker notes from a short brief.
Studytube stores courses, session enrolment and completions.
A language model can draft a role play and a toolbox script from an approved procedure.

risks: A generated script that drops or softens a forklift, VCA or food-safety step is a safety and liability problem.
Plain Dutch from a model can still be too hard for non-native speakers on the floor.
Using a new format to judge people in their probation period will draw works-council attention.
research_questions: What share of these 141 hours is time in the room or on the floor, and what share is preparation?
Which programs require a practical seen by a qualified instructor, so a new format cannot replace that observation?
On one site for four weeks, do crews pass the same practical after the new format pack as they do after today's session?

tasks.short: Write and update handouts, guides and floor cards.

today.trigger: A procedure changes, a Studytube course has no handout, or a team lead asks for a card the floor will use.
steps: Search SharePoint for the SOP and check it is the file the site still uses.
Rewrite it as a guide, a handout or a slide deck in Word or PowerPoint.
Ask a process owner or team lead to confirm the steps.
Store the file on SharePoint and attach it to the Studytube course.
drudgery: Hunting the latest version across three site libraries
Reformatting the same text into a handout, a deck and a pocket card
Retyping warnings that are already in the SOP
today.time_sinks: Writing and layout take the hours. Waiting for someone who knows the aisle to confirm one step adds the delay.

lenses.faster: A pocket card, a handout and a trainer note come out of the approved SOP in the house template. The specialist edits and sends them for sign-off.
lenses.autonomous: A new or changed procedure file on SharePoint opens a draft pack on its own. Nothing is published until a named owner approves it.
lenses.ambitious: Every task the floor and the drivers actually do would have a current one-page card, in the languages those crews use, including for flex workers who start tomorrow.
lenses.joy: Copying procedures into PowerPoint and chasing the old PDF is the part that can go. Choosing the example that matches the Venlo aisle, and the safety step that must stay, is the part that remains.
lenses.options: Three lengths from one source: a wall card, a pocket card and a full guide, plus a plainer-language version for the same steps.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the template, the rule for which file is the source, and the approval path, and reviews packs that fail the check.
reach: Team lead: first draft of task cards they now write from scratch
Recruiter and HR administrator: a starter pack that matches the real procedure
HR business partner: a current leave-behind for a site visit

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which sentence is dangerous if it is shortened, and whether the picture matches the rack, the truck or the hygiene rule on that site.
tasks.pattern_why: The source is an unstructured procedure, the draft is checkable against it, and a person has to approve before floor staff rely on it.

in_practice.trigger: A SharePoint procedure is updated, or a Studytube course has no current handout.
steps: Read the approved SOP, the certificate syllabus if there is one, and the site.
Draft a pocket card, a handout and a trainer note in the house template.
Mark every step that differs from the last approved card.
A named owner approves, and only then is the pack attached to Studytube and the site library.
in_practice.human_gate: Workers do not see the pack until a named process owner has approved the safety-critical steps.
data_needed: Current SOP with an owner and a date
VCA, forklift or food-safety syllabus where the course is mandatory
House template and the word list the floor uses
Languages required per site
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and the Studytube course attachment record.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word drafts a handout from a source document the user supplies inside the tenant.
SharePoint stores versions of a file and can require approval before a version is shared widely.
A summary of a procedure can omit a mandatory step, so a human check against the source remains necessary.

risks: If the SharePoint SOP is older than the card on the wall, the draft spreads the wrong steps to every site.
A short card can drop a lock-out, traffic or hygiene step that the long SOP had.
Photos of named workers in the aisle are personal data under the AVG and do not belong in a prompt or a handout.
Agency staff may also have to follow the agency's instruction, so a Noordhaven-only card can conflict with it.
research_questions: On 10 tasks, how many floor cards differ from the SharePoint SOP in a step the process owner calls mandatory?
In a blind check, what share of drafts omit or change a step the owner marks as mandatory?
Does the Microsoft 365 licence include Copilot, and is procedure content covered by the company data-processing terms?
How many days does a named approver on each site take to sign a one-page card?

tasks.short: Enrol people on the courses their role needs.

today.trigger: A certificate is close to expiry, a hire starts, a team lead reports a skill gap, or an HR business partner asks for training in a reintegration plan under the Wet verbetering poortwachter.
steps: Export certificate dates and completions from Studytube, often into Excel.
Compare them with the AFAS function and site, and with names the team lead writes down.
Tell the person and the manager which course to take, and enrol them in Studytube.
Chase no-shows around shifts. For flex workers, repeat the chase through the agency supervisor.
drudgery: Merging Studytube exports with AFAS and a team-lead spreadsheet
Sending the same reminder to people who were on shift and did not see it
Rebuilding the overdue list because flex names change every week
today.time_sinks: Finding who is overdue, and finding them again after the shift pattern changes, takes longer than the enrolment click.

lenses.faster: The overdue list for VCA, forklift, food safety and week-one modules is ready from AFAS function and Studytube dates. The specialist handles the exceptions and the development conversations.
lenses.autonomous: A certificate nearing its end, or a new contract in AFAS, opens a proposed enrolment. A person confirms it before anyone is booked or marked not deployable.
lenses.ambitious: Permanent staff and seasonal flex workers would hold the certificates for the task they are planned on, and week-one modules would be finished as a normal start.
lenses.joy: Spreadsheet chasing is the part that can go. Talking with a team lead about what a picker still cannot do, and about a reintegration plan, is the part that stays.
lenses.options: For one gap, three offers with hours and cost: a Studytube module, a supervised shift with a buddy, or a classroom date on a day the person is already in.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the rule table of role, task, certificate and renewal, and deals with people who do not fit the rule.
reach: HR administrator: routine enrolment and certificate recording
Recruiter: the courses a new hire must finish in week one, named before the start date
Payroll and compensation: a reliable certificate fact where the CAO links a paper to an allowance
HR business partner: training named in a Wet verbetering poortwachter plan

tasks.human_edge: Seeing when the gap is language, rostering or management, and when a training place will not fix it.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching a recorded certificate to a role is a rule, but enrolling someone or limiting their tasks needs a human confirmation.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly run, plus a new AFAS contract or a Studytube certificate that expires inside the notice window.
steps: Join AFAS function, site and contract to Studytube completions and expiry dates.
List mandatory gaps separately from development offers and from reintegration requests.
A specialist or the manager confirms each enrolment. Flex names that are missing from AFAS go on an exception list for the agency supervisor.
Enrol in Studytube and record the confirmation.
in_practice.human_gate: No enrolment is final, and nobody is marked unfit for a task, until a specialist or the responsible manager confirms it.
data_needed: Signed rule table: function, task, certificate, renewal, practical required or not
Studytube expiry and completion dates
AFAS function, site and contract start
Agency list of flex workers planned on certified tasks
Reintegration actions that name training
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube enrolment record and a weekly exception log on SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Studytube manages enrolments, learning paths and certificate records.
AFAS Profit holds the employee, contract, function and site data a mandatory-training rule needs for own staff.
Unattended enrolment from a function change, covering agency workers who are not in AFAS, is an integration this company has not established.

risks: A rule that only reads AFAS misses most of the 150 to 300 flex workers, who are the seasonal peak.
Marking someone not deployable is an employment decision. The works council should have seen the rule, and a manager confirms the case.
An inferred skill score that restricts tasks would raise EU AI Act questions on employment uses. This stays on recorded certificates and a human confirmation.
A Studytube mail does not reach a night-shift worker who has no time or login on the floor.
research_questions: Where do expiry dates live today, and what share match the card the worker carries?
What share of people doing forklift or food-safe work are agency workers with no AFAS employment record?
Do team leads accept a Monday exception list, or do they plan from their own sheet?
Which CAO articles, if any, tie a certificate to an allowance or to being scheduled on a task?

tasks.short: Record training and judge whether a program worked.

today.trigger: Month end, a management request, or a doubt that a course is worth the shift hours it consumes.
steps: Export Studytube completions, no-shows and certificate status.
Paste them into Excel and add headcount from the AFAS extract.
Ask site managers what they thought, often by mail.
Write a short verdict: keep, change or stop the program.
drudgery: Monthly export and VLOOKUP work
Chasing attendance sheets from classroom days
Reconciling flex names that do not match AFAS employee numbers
today.time_sinks: Assembling the sheet takes longer than deciding. Outcome data beyond attendance is scattered or missing, so the verdict stays thin.

lenses.faster: Completions, no-shows, expiries and week-one status refresh next to the nightly AFAS extract. The specialist writes the verdict, not the table.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly refresh keeps the board current. A program with rising no-shows or failing week-one completion opens a review item. It does not change the program.
lenses.ambitious: Each program would be judged on week-one completion, people still in the job and productive at day 90, and repeat incidents, for every site.
lenses.joy: Stitching exports is the part that can go. The conversation with a site manager about what to stop running is the part that stays.
lenses.options: The same program split by site, shift, permanent or flex, and new hire or refresher, so one weak crew is visible.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the few measures and the review rhythm, and investigates the programs that miss them.
reach: People analytics: a clean training table for the existing HR dashboard
HR business partner: a site view without a one-off extract
HR director: a quarterly keep-or-stop note based on the same figures

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a weak result is a bad course, a roster problem, a language problem, or a small number that means little.
tasks.pattern_why: The figures can be assembled and checked, and a person signs any conclusion that is shared or used to change a program.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly data refresh, with a monthly review and an alert when no-shows or failed week-one completion cross a set line.
steps: Load Studytube completions, expiries and session attendance into the dataset that already refreshes from AFAS.
Cut results by program, site, shift and permanent or flex, at group level.
Draft a short note: what moved, what is too small to read, and what to keep, change or stop.
The specialist edits and signs the note before it goes to the HR director or a site manager.
in_practice.human_gate: Any conclusion shared outside L&D, or any decision to drop or expand a program, is signed by the specialist.
data_needed: Studytube completions and certificate status with a key that matches AFAS
AFAS hire date, site, function and contract type
Agreed group-level definitions for week-one completion and day-90 retention
Incident or quality counts only where the company already trusts the source
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset refresh history and a signed monthly note in SharePoint.

evidence.claim: Power BI refreshes a published dataset on a schedule and the company already refreshes an AFAS extract nightly.
Studytube reports completions and certificate status.
Joining courses to day-90 retention is plausible and easy to over-read when cohorts per site are small.

risks: A clicked-through e-learning module will look successful if completion is the only measure.
Cohorts per site, and the seasonal flex swing, are small, so a day-90 split will move around.
The works council and the AVG constrain person-level learning and performance data. Publish site and team figures.
Forcing agency workers into the employee table will skew retention and absence (verzuim) rates.
research_questions: Can Studytube completions be joined to an AFAS employee number under the current works-council agreement?
For the three largest programs, is there any outcome besides attendance with enough volume per site to compare?
What share of mandatory e-learning is completed without a practical check?
Does finance or operations already keep an incident or damage series L&D is allowed to use?

tasks.short: Design and schedule orientation for starters.

today.trigger: A start date is known from Recruitee or AFAS, a new group of flex workers is ordered, or a site says the current introduction day no longer works.
steps: Copy the last orientation plan and adjust it for the role and the site.
Book Studytube modules, a buddy, a room and any forklift or VCA practical.
Mail the manager, the HR administrator and the trainer with the schedule.
On the day, direct the program and fix clashes with the shift.
After the first week, note who did not finish.
drudgery: Copying last quarter's plan into a new Excel
Emailing five people to find one forklift slot and one buddy
Rebuilding the same list of modules for every picker and every driver
today.time_sinks: Coordination around shifts and scarce buddies takes as long as the design. At peak, flex start dates arrive with little notice.

lenses.faster: A week-one path for a Tilburg picker or a Venlo driver, with modules, buddy shifts and certificate bookings, is drafted from the last approved path. The specialist confirms capacity.
lenses.autonomous: An accepted offer in Recruitee, or a new contract in AFAS, opens a site-specific checklist. Rooms, buddies and practicals are proposed and stay unbooked until a person confirms.
lenses.ambitious: Every hire, and every flex worker who will stay more than a few days, would get a complete week-one path at peak as well as in a quiet month.
lenses.joy: Copying the old plan and chasing a truck slot by mail is the part that can go. Deciding what someone must be able to do on day five is the part that stays.
lenses.options: Three week-one paths: Dutch-speaking permanent hire, non-Dutch flex worker, and internal move, each with buddy hours and cost.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the standard paths per role and site, and reviews the cohorts that miss week one or day 90.
reach: Recruiter: a first-week story that is true, told before the offer
HR administrator: the booking list they now assemble by hand
HR business partner: a site comparison when early leaving clusters in one orientation

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which site has no buddy on nights, and what team leads will actually run when the floor is busy.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist remains responsible for the path, because site capacity, shift design and the day-90 goal are judgments a draft cannot settle.

in_practice.trigger: Offer accepted in Recruitee, contract created in AFAS, or a flex order that names a start date.
steps: Select the standard path for the role, site and contract type.
Draft the week-one schedule: Studytube modules, buddy shifts, practicals and the name of the manager.
The specialist or the site manager confirms buddy and truck capacity before anything is promised.
Publish the checklist to the manager and the HR administrator, and track finishers in Studytube.
in_practice.human_gate: No starter is promised a practical, a buddy or a deployable status until the site confirms capacity.
data_needed: Standard path per large role and site
Start date, site, function and language
Buddy and practical capacity for that week
Modules that count as week-one complete
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint orientation checklist and Studytube completion for the week-one path.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word drafts a plan from a previous orientation document.
Studytube can hold the e-learning modules of a week-one path and record who finished them.
Recruitee records offers and AFAS records the employee after hire. An automatic handoff between them is not established for this company.

risks: A full plan that ignores night-shift buddy and truck time will be ignored on the floor.
The offer can sit in Recruitee for days before an AFAS contract exists, so a trigger on AFAS is late for someone who starts Monday.
Changing how probation is assessed in week one needs a check with HR and the works council.
Peak flex volume can be several times the permanent starter volume, and a path built for permanent hires will not fit.
research_questions: For the five largest roles, is there a written week-one path, and how often was it followed last quarter?
How many starters arrive per site per week at peak, and how many buddies are available on the night shift?
What share of new hires finish the required Studytube modules in week one today?
How many days typically pass between a Recruitee offer acceptance and an AFAS contract?

tasks.short: Compare classroom, online and floor delivery.

today.trigger: Someone asks whether a program can move online, a vendor quote arrives, or the three sites are travelling to one classroom again.
steps: Pull completion and attendance from Studytube and classroom sheets.
Estimate trainer hours, travel between Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, and the shift cover the site must arrange.
Check whether the certificate body expects a practical.
Recommend a mode in a mail or a slide, usually for one program at a time.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same cost comparison in Excel for each request
Chasing travel costs and backfill estimates that are not in one place
Repeating the argument that a practical cannot be a video
today.time_sinks: The hours go to gathering cost and cover, not to the choice. Each request starts from a blank sheet.

lenses.faster: Trainer hours, travel, backfill, vendor cost and completion by mode sit on one sheet drawn from Studytube and finance figures. The recommendation is still written by the specialist.
lenses.autonomous: When a program is scheduled, cost per completer by mode refreshes. The mode does not change on its own.
lenses.ambitious: The company would pick the mode per crew and per certificate rule, and would stop bringing three sites to Rotterdam for a topic a supervised toolbox talk can carry.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the 'can this be online?' spreadsheet is the part that can go. Deciding what must stay hands-on is the part that stays.
lenses.options: Five mixes for one program, each with trainer hours, travel, lost shift hours, expected completion and a yes or no on the practical requirement.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the decision rule: hands-on where the certificate, the insurer or the task requires it, and the cheapest competent mode otherwise. Exceptions come back for review.
reach: Controller and FP&A analyst: training cost per completer in figures they can reconcile
HR business partner: the backfill consequence for a site, before the date is fixed
Procurement of vendors: a written reason when a classroom quote is declined

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which part of VCA or forklift training the certificate body and the insurer require in person, and when a quiet floor still cannot release people for e-learning.
tasks.pattern_why: The comparison can be drafted from data, and the specialist remains responsible for a recommendation that affects safety, cover and cost.

in_practice.trigger: A program is up for renewal, a vendor quote arrives, or a site asks to change the mode.
steps: Load completion, attendance, trainer hours, travel and vendor cost for the last runs.
Add the practical rule: required in person, theory allowed online, or no certificate constraint.
Draft up to five mixes with cost per completer and shift hours lost.
The specialist recommends one mix and records why the others fell away.
in_practice.human_gate: The delivery mode changes only after the specialist signs the recommendation. Safety and certificate programs also need the process owner.
data_needed: Completions and attendance by activity
Trainer hours, vendor invoices and travel cost
Backfill or lost-shift estimate from the site
Certificate-body rule for theory and practical
in_practice.logs_to: A signed mode decision in the SharePoint course folder, with the comparison sheet attached.

evidence.claim: Studytube reports completions for digital modules, and classroom attendance can be stored against the same course.
Power BI can compare hours and cost once those amounts are in a dataset.
VCA and forklift qualifications include practical requirements that a cost comparison cannot override.

risks: A cost model that leaves out backfill will make e-learning look cheaper than it is for the site.
Certificate-body and insurer rules fix some hours as in-person. A virtual practical is not an available option there.
Whether e-learning is paid working time matters under the CAO and to the works council.
Travel and emissions figures are thin and stay a side column beside safety and cost.
research_questions: For each mandatory program, does the certificate body or the insurer require in-person hours or a practical test?
Are trainer hours, travel and shift backfill posted to a cost centre finance can split by program?
Do night-shift workers have paid time and a working Studytube login, confirmed by the three site managers?
How often was the mode changed last year, and did completion or incidents move afterwards?

tasks.short: Read what changed in certificates, CAO and training.

today.trigger: Newsletters, CAO updates, vendor mail and syllabus news arrive through the week, and the specialist reads them between sessions.
steps: Skim Outlook for CAO news, VCA and forklift syllabus items, Studytube release notes and training articles.
Open the few PDFs that look serious.
Mention a relevant change to the other specialist or an HR business partner.
Sometimes update a course later, when someone remembers.
drudgery: Vendor mail and generic leadership articles
Losing a PDF that arrived three weeks ago
Retelling the same CAO point to several colleagues
today.time_sinks: The volume of low-value mail hides the rare syllabus or CAO change that should alter a program. There is no fixed slot for the reading, so it slips.

lenses.faster: A Monday brief covers a closed list: warehouse CAO and CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer updates, VCA and forklift syllabus, food-safety rules, Studytube changes, and AVG or works-council practice on training. The specialist reads that brief.
lenses.autonomous: The brief runs every Monday from the closed source list. It changes no course and books no one.
lenses.ambitious: Programs would be updated in the same month a syllabus or CAO rule changes, on all three sites, including the flex induction.
lenses.joy: Skimming vendor mail is the part that can go. Reading one primary text the specialist chose, and talking it through with a colleague, is the part that stays.
lenses.options: Each item arrives as three lines: what changed, which course or certificate it touches, and whether the primary PDF must be opened.
lenses.altitude: The specialist curates the source list and the rule for which items must be read in full, and samples the brief for misses.
reach: Compensation and benefits: CAO items that mention allowances or certificates
HR business partner: training and reintegration items under the Wet verbetering poortwachter
HR administrator: certificate-rule changes that affect filing

tasks.human_edge: Telling marketing from a change that alters a certificate, a CAO obligation or a program the floor is running this month.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured mail and PDFs become a short sourced brief inside a fixed weekly workflow, and a person checks anything that would change a course.

in_practice.trigger: Every Monday, from a source list the specialist maintains.
steps: Collect new items from the closed list only.
Produce a one-page brief: change, source, date, and which Noordhaven program it might touch.
The specialist opens the primary text for anything that would change a course, a certificate rule or a CAO-related practice.
Accepted items are written to a change log. The rest are dropped.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing in the brief changes a program, a rule table or a message to the works council until the specialist has opened the source and accepted the item.
data_needed: Closed list of sources and owners
Current course and certificate list so items can be matched
A place to store the primary PDF next to the brief
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint change log with the source link, the date read, and the specialist's accept or drop.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can summarise an Outlook thread or a newsletter the mailbox already holds.
A fixed Dutch source list can be turned into a weekly brief of syllabus, CAO and tool changes.
Summaries of legal and syllabus PDFs can miss the operative sentence, so the primary text still has to be opened before a program changes.

risks: A brief can drop the one clause in a CAO protocol or a VCA syllabus that should change a course.
If the source list is open, vendor mail will crowd out certificate-body and CAO items.
Acting on the brief without the primary PDF will eventually put a wrong step into a floor card.
Copying a full CAO or syllabus file into a personal chatbot sits outside the company AVG arrangement.
research_questions: Which external changes in the past 24 months forced a rewrite of a Noordhaven course, and which source carried them?
How many minutes a week do the two specialists spend on this reading, measured over two ordinary weeks?
In a four-week trial, what share of brief items are irrelevant, wrong, or missing a change the prevention contact noticed independently?
Is there already a CAO or safety update path through HR or the site that this brief would duplicate?

tasks.short: Check trainers' outlines and handouts against the standard.

today.trigger: An external trainer sends a deck, or a team lead submits a toolbox sheet, before a course is allowed to run.
steps: Read the outline, text or handout against the SharePoint SOP and the certificate syllabus.
Mark wrong steps, old screens and language the floor will not follow.
Mail the trainer with the changes.
File the approved version on SharePoint and in Studytube.
drudgery: Page-by-page comparison with a long SOP
Repeating the same comments on house style and reading level
Losing track of which version the trainer sent back
today.time_sinks: Reading a long vendor deck end to end, most of which is unchanged from last year, takes the time. The real finds are usually a handful of steps.

lenses.faster: The pack is checked against the current SOP, the syllabus and a reading-level rule, and the specialist reads the flagged pages. The verdict stays with the specialist.
lenses.autonomous: A file dropped in the SharePoint review library starts the check. The comment to the trainer is not sent until the specialist accepts it.
lenses.ambitious: Every external VCA, forklift and food-safety pack, and every site-made toolbox sheet, would be reviewed the same way, including the ones that now go out unread.
lenses.joy: Line-by-line comparison with the SOP is the part that can go. The conversation with a trainer who disagrees, and the final yes, stay with the specialist.
lenses.options: The review returns a must-fix list, a could-improve list, and a plain-Dutch rewrite of the worst page, for the specialist to accept or ignore.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the rubric and samples packs afterwards, and reads in full only the packs the check flags or the courses that are safety-critical.
reach: Team lead: a check of task cards before they are printed for the aisle
HR administrator: a check of starter sheets they assemble from old files
Procurement: a written defect list when a vendor pack is rejected

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a flagged line is a real safety miss or a fair simplification, and keeping a usable relationship with a trainer the sites trust.
tasks.pattern_why: A handout is unstructured input and the rubric produces a checkable defect list, which a person accepts before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: A trainer or team lead uploads an outline, deck or handout to the SharePoint review library.
steps: Compare the pack with the current SOP, the certificate syllabus and the rubric.
Return page-referenced must-fix and could-improve points, each tied to a source line.
The specialist reads every must-fix point and the surrounding page, then accepts or drops it.
The specialist sends the comment and files the approved version on Studytube.
in_practice.human_gate: No pack is approved or rejected, and no comment goes to a trainer, until the specialist has accepted the defect list.
data_needed: Written rubric: mandatory steps, syllabus coverage, reading level, named source, no worker scoring
Current SOP and syllabus
The submitted pack and its version
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint review library: submitted file, defect list, specialist decision and date.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Word can draft comments on a document held in the company tenant.
A language model can mark a handout against a written rubric and a source SOP and return page-referenced points.
Fluent text with a missing safety step is a known way document review by a model fails.

risks: A fluent pack that skipped a safety or hygiene step can still look fine on style and structure.
If the SOP used as the standard is wrong, every review will enforce the wrong step.
Comments that sound mechanical will sour external trainers the sites still need.
Names, photos and medical details in example material are personal data under the AVG and should stay in the company tenant.
research_questions: How many internal and external packs were reviewed in the last year, and how many hours did each take?
On 15 old packs, how many checklist findings does a specialist call real, and how many known defects does the checklist miss?
Do current trainer contracts allow Noordhaven to require changes before a course runs?
Is there a written rubric today, or does each specialist judge from experience?

role.altitude: The role owns the system that gets someone productive and still here at day 90: the certificate rules, the week-one paths per role and site, the material standard, and the review of which programs change retention, absence and repeat incidents. The two specialists spend their own time on design, approval and the crews that miss that bar.
reach: Recruiter: a true first-week story in Recruitee before the offer is made
HR administrator: routine Studytube enrolment and certificate chasing for own staff
People analytics: the training measures on the nightly HR dashboard
HR business partner: site certificate and week-one gaps for the quarterly conversation, and training named in a Wet verbetering poortwachter plan
Controller and FP&A: training cost per completer by delivery mode, from figures finance already holds
Team leads: a first draft of task cards, which the lead still signs
role.ceiling_note: Two people cannot cover Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo on every shift. Practical exams, floor coaching and trust with team leads stay in person. Peak season adds up to 300 flex workers who often sit outside AFAS, and that volume caps any path built only on employee records. Certificate-body rules, the CAO and the works council limit unattended enrolment and any use of learning data to judge a worker. These eight tasks are about half of the role; vendor management, coaching and reintegration support still take the rest.
skills_to_grow: Write a certificate rule table, with role, task, renewal and whether a practical is required, that Studytube and AFAS can run
Read Power BI cuts by site, shift and flex, and state what a small cohort cannot prove
Edit plain Dutch at the reading level of the warehouse, including for non-native speakers
Check VCA, forklift and food-safety materials against the current syllabus and the actual site
Apply works-council practice and the AVG when learning data is tied to a person, and keep employment-related uses on recorded facts with a human confirmation
role.ambitious_version: Both specialists keep permanent staff and flex workers qualified for the task they are planned on, see every starter finish a real week-one path, and put their own hours into the crews and programs that miss day 90 or repeat the same incidents. Handouts, overdue lists and delivery comparisons run with a person approving anything that is safety-critical or that changes someone's work.
